ruleName: Developer-conference programme grouping sessions into three tracks, where each session card's track is shown ONLY by its background hue (blue/amber/green) with a colour legend but NO per-card 'T1/T2/T3' text code — the canonical G14 colour-coded-schedule example with the text code removed.

Restaurant lunch menu where dish spice level is conveyed solely by dish-name colour (green = mild, red = spicy) with the two hues deliberately at the SAME lightness (~1.06:1 between them) and no icon/word per dish. The discriminating twin of case-01: same concept, no lightness gap, so it FAILS.

Retail-banking transaction list where credits are light-green and debits are dark-red text (large-bold). The two foreground colours differ in hue AND by ~3.15:1 in lightness between each other, so the lightness difference is an additional visual distinction and the page PASSES via the escape hatch (a naive 'colour cue = fail' would wrongly flag it).

TRUE NEGATIVE: light-rail weekend departures TABLE where service tracks are shown by background hue AND every departure carries an in-text '· T1 / · T2 / · T3' code after the destination, with a legend tying each code to its line. The G14 sufficient colour-coded-schedule pattern; the passing boundary for case-04.

SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

Cinema showtime picker (radio-as-pills) where the chosen showtime is distinguished by inverting the pill's foreground and background (unselected dark-text-on-white; selected white-text-on-dark). The inversion is an additional visual distinction with ~15.7:1 lightness difference, so it PASSES.

Newsroom investigations archive where article links are underlined (distinguished from static text by a non-colour cue) and visited vs unvisited links differ by colour only, with ~1.09:1 contrast between the two link colours (below 3:1). PASSES via the visited-link exemption.

ruleName: Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

Fintech dashboard: an SVG line chart of daily NAV where each <circle> data point shows a detail pop-up on mouseenter, offset above-and-right of the point. Points are closely spaced (~26px) and share one reusable pop-up. To read the offset pop-up for a point under magnification, the pointer must travel toward it — crossing the next data point, whose mouseenter replaces the wanted pop-up with the neighbour's (the exact F95 chart example).

E-commerce category sidebar: hovering a top-level category ("Camp & Hike") reveals a CSS-only flyout submenu offset to the right (left:230px against a 210px row, leaving a ~20px transparent corridor). The flyout is a DOM child of the category but not geometrically contiguous; reaching lower submenu items requires a diagonal down-and-right path that exits both hot-zones, ending the :hover state and collapsing the flyout before the cursor arrives.

Cloud-platform status console with a 'Region health' matrix where each region/service state (operational/degraded/major outage) is shown only by the hue of an identically-shaped green/amber/red dot. Meaning depends on perceiving the specific hue, so it FAILS; a sibling 'Active incidents' list that adds text badges is the passing contrast.

Northwind Pharmacy refill queue: each status help icon shipped with a native title=, but a Bootstrap/jQuery-UI-style tooltip plugin strips the native title on load (removeAttribute('title')) and renders its own gray span.nwtip styled to mimic the native UA tooltip. The author bubble is pointer-events:none, toggled only on mouseenter/mouseleave of the 18px icon, with no Escape handler. Visually near-identical to the case-01 native tooltip, but author-owned, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip on the parking-zone help button satisfies all three 1.4.13 obligations: it is dismissible via Escape, remains visible when the pointer travels onto it, and persists until explicitly dismissed.

ruleName: Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

Helios Energy kWh bar chart: each SVG rect bar has an SVG <title> child (UA-rendered native tooltip, e.g. 'February: 612 kWh', out of scope) AND an author .vtip floating overlay shown on hover with DIFFERENT, richer text ('Feb · 612 kWh · $84.10 · 18% below your 12-mo avg'). The overlay is pointer-events:none, repositions under the cursor via mousemove, and has no Escape handler. Two on-hover sources, two owners, two divergent texts — the reviewer must separate which content the SC governs (only the author overlay) and judge its behavior.

Aurora Transit trip planner: each leg has a round service-note icon where the author sets title='' to suppress the native tooltip, then paints an identical gray bubble with a pure-CSS ::after { content: attr(data-hint) } (no JavaScript). The bubble appears only while the 22px icon itself is :hovered; a ::after pseudo-element cannot receive the pointer and there is no Escape affordance. Indistinguishable from a native tooltip, but author CSS owns it, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

ruleName: E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

Collaborative document editor with a sync chip: on hover/focus it shows a persistent role=tooltip detail that meets all three conditions; separately, while editing, a transient 'Saving…' busy state appears, changes to 'Saved.' on completion, then settles. ruleName: Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

Arabic RTL airline seat-selection page: a held seat (C٢) shows, on hover/focus, a role=tooltip with the live remaining hold time (Arabic-Indic countdown). Government DMV registration-renewal wizard: focus-triggered help bubbles (role=tooltip) under the Plate and VIN fields. A single global setInterval(...,5000) clears any visible bubble every 5 seconds, so the VIN help vanishes while the field still has focus and the user is mid-task. Verified: visible on focus -> display:none at 6s while document.activeElement is still #vin.

ruleName: Northwind Mutual privacy policy (data-retention section): the glossary term 'legal hold' is a focusable inline <button> whose definition popup carries unique material content (data may be retained beyond normal windows and despite a deletion request). Built correctly: revealed on BOTH focusin and mouseenter (keyboard/pointer parity), dismissible with Escape without moving focus, and hoverable/persistent. Conforming counter-fixture → PASS.

Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

SaaS onboarding coachmark embedded as a cross-document <iframe src='case-01-frame.html'>. The embedded mini-app's only control, a 'Got it' button, swallows Tab (keydown preventDefault + self-refocus) and re-grabs focus onblur, so focus enters the iframe and can never cross back to the parent's 'Open dashboard' link. No Esc, no exit advice.

Nonprofit donation page with a hosted-card-fields-style payment widget in a cross-document <iframe>. The embedded form re-implements its own tab cycle: the last control ('Donate $25') loops forward Tab back to the first field, and Shift+Tab from the first field loops to the last, so Tab cycles among the widget's controls forever and never crosses the iframe boundary to the parent's 'Cancel and return to home' link. No exit advice.

Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. The reveal is the selector abbr.term:hover .bubble with no JS, so keyboard focus structurally cannot reveal it; the author also set tabindex="-1", removing the <abbr> from the tab order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The 'TBA' tooltip fails 1.4.13 on two counts: it disappears when the pointer moves from the trigger onto the tooltip (not hoverable), and pressing Escape while the trigger is hovered does not dismiss it (not dismissable).

ruleName: Cedar Valley Health patient portal A1C trend chart: five hemoglobin A1C results are drawn as absolutely-positioned <div> markers; hovering reveals a popup with the exact value, date, and the provider's per-result clinical note (e.g. dose increased to 1000mg, recheck in 3 months). Those values and notes appear only in the hover popups (no data-table fallback). Markers are non-focusable <div>s with mouseenter/mouseleave-only popups, so keyboard users can read none of the data.

Forum thread reply box implemented as a custom element <comment-composer> whose UI lives in an open Shadow DOM (attachShadow mode:open, delegatesFocus:true). The light-DOM source is just the empty custom-element tag. The component listens for focusout on its shadow root and synchronously re-focuses the textarea, so Tab/Shift+Tab cycle textarea<->button forever and never cross the shadow boundary to the parent's 'Back to all threads' link. No Esc, no advice.

Podcast episode page embeds an audio-controls panel as a cross-document <iframe>. Inside are real focusable controls (Play/Pause, Rewind, Forward, seek slider, speed select). The player adds legitimate widget behavior (Play toggles label; range uses native arrows) but does NOT intercept Tab anywhere, so forward Tab on the last control falls through and crosses the iframe boundary to the parent's 'Show transcript' link. PASS boundary variant (G21 mechanism #1).

Transit service-update page embeds an interactive route diagram as a separate SVG document via <object type='image/svg+xml' data='case-05-map.svg'>. The SVG's four focusable station <a> links are looped by the SVG's own script (last->first on forward Tab, first->last on Shift+Tab) so Tab never crosses the object boundary to the parent's 'Next: fares & passes' link. A paragraph BEFORE the object reads 'Tab through the diagram, then press Tab once more to continue' — plausible G21-style advice that is in fact FALSE.

Knowledge-base Markdown editor as a custom element <markdown-editor> in an open Shadow DOM. Inside the textarea Tab is deliberately captured to insert indentation (the WCAG rich-text-editor example), so plain Tab does not advance focus. BUT a persistent visible instruction inside the shadow root says 'Press Esc to leave the editor', and a working Esc handler blurs the textarea and moves focus across the shadow boundary to the host 'Publish' button. PASS boundary variant.

Government DMV vehicle-registration renewal modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). Focus IS restricted to the dialog (Tab wraps among its controls), but this is the legitimate-containment carve-out: a wired, functional Esc handler closes the dialog and restores focus to the triggering button, and the focus cycle explicitly includes the focusable header Close (✕) and footer Cancel. The conformant modal the ACT corpus never models.

Long-form magazine newsletter gate built with the HTML popover attribute (popover="manual"). On load it pops open and grabs focus; a document focusin guard snaps focus back to the email field whenever it tries to leave (hand-built trap on top of the popover). It displays 'Not now? Press Esc to dismiss' but NO Esc listener is wired, and popover="manual" disables the UA's native light-dismiss/Esc-close, so the documented exit is false.

SaaS analytics dashboard 'Create alert rule' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). It HAS a genuine focusable header Close button and footer Cancel button, but the hand-rolled focus trap was scoped to a hard-coded selector ('.dialog-form input/select/button') that matches only the form-body controls, so the wrap cycle excludes both dismiss controls. The user can see Close/Cancel but Tab can never land on them; no Esc handler either.

Cobalt Bank account-opening flow with ONE modal that is conformant containment in isolation: 'Verify your identity' opens a role=dialog aria-modal=true overlay, initial focus lands on a real focusable Close button, an Escape handler on the parent document closes it, Close/Cancel/Continue sit in the Tab cycle, and focus is restored to the opener. The defect is the embedded third-party format in the modal body: a 'SecureScan' KYC widget delivered as an <iframe srcdoc> second document whose own Tab-wrap and focusin re-grab keep focus circulating inside the frame forever, while the modal's Escape listener - living one document up - never receives keydowns fired inside the frame. A keyboard user can enter the verification step but cannot leave it.

E-commerce (outdoor retail) product 'Quick view' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). A focus trap cycles Tab among the size/quantity/Add-to-cart controls. The only dismiss is a round '✕' that is a <span> with role=button + aria-label and an onclick handler only — not focusable (no tabindex, not a real button) and with no keydown; there is also no Esc handler. Closeable by mouse, trapped by keyboard.

SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

ruleName: Restaurant online-ordering 'Browse menu' dropdown built as an APG role=menu with roving tabindex; arrows move among dishes but the keydown handler also preventDefault()s Tab/Shift+Tab and remaps them to item movement, so once focus enters the open menu it can never reach the promo field or the checkout button. RTL Arabic real-estate filter page (دار السكن) with two visually and structurally identical ARIA listboxes. The left 'Area' listbox releases focus when arrowing past the ends (standard arrow-key exit, no advice owed = PASS foil); the right 'Property type' listbox clamps the arrows and only escapes via the undocumented non-standard combo Ctrl+Shift+X with no advice = FAIL. Flight-booking departure-date picker built as an ARIA role=grid calendar (the canonical Understanding 'calendar widget' construct). Arrows navigate day cells, but the grid keydown handler captures BOTH Tab and Shift+Tab with preventDefault() 'to keep focus in the calendar until a date is picked', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus can never reach the Search flights button.

Online-banking step-up OTP verification modal (Meridian Credit Union). It DISPLAYS the advice 'Press Esc to cancel and return to your account', but the keydown handler compares e.keyCode === 13 (Enter; Esc is 27) by mistake, so the documented standard exit key never fires — advice and implementation disagree.

SaaS analytics dashboard with a valid APG role=tablist (MRR/Churn/Cohorts/Forecast). Arrows move between tabs and Tab is NOT preventDefault'd, but each tab has a blur listener that refocuses the active tab on the next tick (setTimeout(()=>tab.focus())), so pressing Tab to leave the tablist toward the panel link or the Export button instantly snaps focus back to the tab.

Theatre box-office seat-picker modal (Aurora Hall). Both Esc and Close release focus, but the promo-code <input> calls stopPropagation() on its keydown, so Escape never reaches the dialog handler WHEN that field is focused. Esc works from the seat buttons and silently fails from the input — a positional trap that requires testing exit from EACH focus position.

E-commerce headphones store with a custom div role=slider 'Max price' facet. Arrows (and PageUp/Down, Home/End) adjust the price with complete ARIA value semantics, but the thumb keydown handler also captures Tab with preventDefault() 'to prevent accidental value loss when you tab away mid-drag', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus is stranded on the thumb and cannot reach Apply, the brand checkboxes, or the product links.

Job-application form with a roving-tabindex role=listbox ('How did you hear about this role?'). Arrows navigate options and Enter selects; the keydown handler deliberately omits any Tab case, so unmodified Tab carries focus OUT to the Submit button and Shift+Tab back to the Email field. The on-screen help wrongly says 'Use Tab to move between options' — a misleading mental model, but NOT a 2.1.2 failure because Tab still exits. Boundary PASS case.

RTL Arabic article-publishing editor with an APG role=toolbar (Bold/Italic/Underline/List/Link) using roving tabindex and aria-pressed toggles. In RTL, ArrowLeft advances; the handler also captures Tab and the movement WRAPS, so at the last button advancing loops back to the first instead of exiting — a closed within-widget loop with no exit index. ruleName: Coffee storefront header cart 'X items in cart' wrapped in role=status; clicking Add to cart rewrites ONLY the inner <span id=cart-count> 0->3 while the region has no aria-atomic, so AT announces a bare 'three' instead of 'three items in cart'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The refill status message 'You have 2 refills remaining' is only announced as the bare number '2' to AT due to aria-atomic="false" on the role="status" container, making the live announcement semantically incomplete and meaningless without

ruleName: Financial-news long-form article with a sticky 'Watchlist' price ticker in the right rail. The ticker is a present, valid live region wired aria-live=assertive, and a setInterval re-prices NDX/SPX/BTC every 2 seconds. For a screen-reader user reading the article, the price tape assertively interrupts the narration every two seconds, indefinitely. A ticking price board is the textbook low-value, high-frequency status SCR14 says should be polite and toggleable.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The price-ticker live region uses aria-live="assertive" for non-urgent, frequently-repeating price updates, interrupting screen-reader users every ~2 seconds and constituting a 4.1.3 barrier due to inappropriate politeness.

ruleName:
City recycling-bin request form: on submit the handler does resultArea.innerHTML = '

', so the role=status attribute is born inside the same markup string as the confirmation text. The resting DOM is a textbook-correct live region but no live region existed at page load.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The 'Now playing' status message is correctly conveyed to assistive technology via a pre-existing role='status' live region with aria-atomic='true', which announces the full updated text politely when the track changes.

ruleName: Arabic RTL library catalogue with result count 'النتائج: ٠ نتيجة' (Results: 0 result) in p[role=status]; each search rewrites ONLY the inner <b id=n> Eastern-Arabic numeral while the region is non-atomic, so AT announces a bare '٢٤' having dropped both the leading 'results:' label and the trailing 'result(s)' unit.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The result-count paragraph carries role='status' (a pre-existing polite live region) and the screen reader announces the full string 'النتائج: ٦ نتيجة' after a search — conveying the status message to AT without requiring focus.

ruleName: Hiking-boot faceted store with a result summary 'Showing 38 products' inside aria-live=polite; toggling a filter rewrites ONLY the inner <b id=count> numeral while the region is non-atomic (aria-atomic defaults to false for explicit aria-live), so AT announces a context-free '24'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The product-count status message is conveyed visually as 'Showing 29 products' but AT receives only the bare numeral ('29') because the live region lacks aria-atomic='true' and AJAX rewrites only the inner <b> child.

ruleName: Legal case-management document upload with 'Uploading: 0% complete' in p[role=status][aria-atomic=false]; a timer rewrites ONLY the inner <span id=pct> percentage node, so AT announces a bare '85' (verified live: pct moved to 12 while visible string stayed 'Uploading: 12% complete') with no 'percent complete'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The upload-progress status message is announced by AT only as bare numbers ('9', '21', '30'…) with no surrounding context, because aria-atomic="false" restricts announcement to the mutated child span alone, making the message unintelligible

ruleName: University library catalog same-page search: #results ships as a plain div with no aria-live; on submit render() calls box.setAttribute('aria-live','polite') and writes the '7 results found' status line + hits into the same element in one synchronous operation, so aria-live is upgraded onto the element at the same tick it is filled.

RTL Arabic pharmacy refill portal (novel long-tail + i18n): each Renew button clones a <template> whose content node ALREADY carries role=status, aria-live=polite, and the Arabic confirmation copy; cloneNode(true) then appendChild inserts a born-with-content live region. ruleName: SaaS analytics 'Run now' dashboard with a hand-rolled toast helper: showToast() does document.createElement('div'), setAttribute('role','status') and aria-live='polite', sets two text children, and ONLY THEN appendChild()s the finished element. Region and message arrive in one tick on a node that was detached until connection.

E-commerce hiking-gear store: a valid role=status/aria-live=polite/aria-atomic=true cart badge updates from 0 to 1/2/3 on Add-to-Cart, announcing only the bare number. The word 'cart' that gives the number meaning lives on the adjacent icon glyph's aria-label (so 1.1.1 passes) but sits outside the atomic region and is never re-read on update.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The cart count badge is a properly configured, pre-existing polite live region that is confirmed by screen-reader to announce its updated value when items are added to the cart.

ruleName: Real-time stock-price watchlist (novel long-tail): when a price-alert threshold is crossed the app mounts a custom element <price-alert>, whose connectedCallback createElement('div'), sets role=status and aria-live=assertive, sets textContent to the alert, and appends it — assembling a filled live region as the element enters the DOM via the custom-element lifecycle.

SaaS CRM leads pipeline grid. Changing a row's Stage select autosaves and injects 'Saved ✓' into that row's own per-row valid live region. The whole string is announced atomically, but it names only the action — never which lead. The lead identity is conveyed only by which visual row the green checkmark lands in.

Auto-parts AJAX 'Parts finder': a 'Searching the catalog…' spinner is announced in a role=status polite live region on entry, then the region is emptied on completion and the result rows plus an '8 matches found' count are injected into a separate non-live <section>. The disappearing spinner is the only 'done' cue; AT hears neither the end of the wait nor the count.

Photo-management app viewing the 'Wedding' album. Saving a photo fires a bottom-center toast (valid role=status/aria-atomic, present before action) that shows a check + 'Saved'. The destination album name is in the top bar and active sidebar item the toast visually floats over, but the announcement omits it — the verbatim Understanding 'Saved in Wedding album' case.

LMS reflective-essay editor (contenteditable) autosaves. A 'Saving your changes…' pill is announced in a top-bar role=status polite region on entry, then on success the pill is simply removed and the save-status area goes blank — no 'All changes saved' replacement. Sighted users infer success from the pill vanishing; AT users hear 'Saving…' then permanent silence and cannot tell if the draft saved before the deadline.

RTL Arabic (dir=rtl, lang=ar) fintech stock watchlist. Each row's Change cell is its own valid live region. Refreshing prices writes the new percentage (e.g. '+2.3%') into each region, announced in full — but with no ticker symbol. Which equity moved is conveyed only by which row (the symbol in the first column) the change sits beside.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The percentage-change cell carries role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true", pre-exists the update, and the screen reader verbatim confirms a polite announcement (+2.3% for row 1) fires when prices are refreshed.

ruleName: PASS boundary control. Government 2FA identity step: 'Sending verification code…' is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then the SAME region is overwritten in-place with '✓ Code sent to the mobile number ending 47. Enter it below.' (announced), and the OTP input is revealed. The end of the wait is announced by REPLACING the busy text, not by silently removing it — the correct 'Removal of status text' remediation.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The status message is correctly conveyed to assistive technology through a pre-existing polite live region, with a confirmed screen-reader announcement on activation.

ruleName: Restaurant reservation widget: 'Checking availability…' plus a spinner is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on success the busy region is emptied and a previously-disabled 'Reserve this table' button is enabled (its label unchanged). Sighted users read the spinner vanishing + the greyed button lighting up as 'a table is available'; AT users hear 'Checking availability…' then silence, with no 'Available — you can book' status and only a bare disabled→enabled control flip.

Concert-ticketing seat map (rows 12–15, seats A–H). Each seat button has a complete accessible name and valid aria-pressed. Selecting a seat turns it green and writes 'Selected' into a shared valid live region — never 'Seat 14C selected'. Which seat is conveyed only by which grid cell changed color.

Bilingual pharmacy refill: 'Checking insurance coverage…' plus a spinner is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on completion the busy region is emptied and a plain #priceOut block ('Your copay: $12.00 · Covered by BlueShield Select PPO · 88% paid') is revealed with no role=status/aria-live. The copay outcome is itself a status message yet is conveyed visually only, and the end of the wait is silent — a decision-blocking gap on a health-and-cost page.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The status message ('Checking insurance coverage…') is correctly conveyed to assistive technology via a pre-existing polite live region — no barrier exists.

ruleName: Candle-shop checkout: 'Processing payment…' plus an indeterminate progress bar is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on success the busy region is emptied AND a brand-new confirmation panel ('Thank you — your order is confirmed', Order #LUM-50418) is revealed as an ordinary <div> with no role=status/aria-live. AT hears 'Processing payment…' then silence — neither the end of the wait nor whether the card was charged, risking a duplicate charge if they re-press.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The payment processing status message is correctly conveyed to assistive technology via a pre-existing polite live region and is verbatim announced by the screen reader.

ruleName: SaaS pricing page with three plan columns (Starter/Team/Business). A team-size select recomputes the best plan, moves a green 'Best value' ribbon to the winning column, and updates a shared valid live region — to just 'Best value'. Which plan won is conveyed only by which column heading the ribbon visually sits over; the ribbon itself is aria-hidden.

ruleName: PASS boundary control: a food-ordering confirmation toast (Saffron Kitchen). On Place order, a present role="alert" plays a success chime and shows a green check icon (aria-hidden), but co-locates a meaningful text node — 'Order placed — Confirmation #SK-4471 · ready ~6:45 PM' — inside the same atomic region, so the present live region announces a real status.

LMS assignment-upload widget (Cell Biology 210). A spinner is injected into a present role="status" region on submit (busy), then swapped for a green-check on completion (done). The image swap is the only busy/success indicator.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The pre-existing role='status' live region fires after Submit but announces only empty content, while the visible status update text appears outside the live region — AT users receive no meaningful status announcement.

ruleName: Insurance auto-quote wizard (step 2 of 5). Inline licence-number validation swaps a neutral gray dot to a red 'X' SVG inside a present role="alert" region on invalid submit. The alert fires but its only child is an aria-hidden SVG with no text, so it announces an empty string.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The validation status indicator uses a pre-existing role='alert' container, but populates it only with an aria-hidden SVG icon — no text is ever inserted into the live region, so AT users receive no announcement of the validation status.

ruleName: Municipal CMS rich-text page editor with an autosave indicator. On Save, the aria-live="polite" indicator's DOM text is cleared and the 'Saved' state is conveyed purely by a CSS rule .saved::after { content: "\2713" } that paints a green check via generated content.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The save-state span uses a pre-existing aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" region and the screen reader confirms it announces status updates ("Saving") without requiring focus movement.

ruleName: CI/CD pipeline dashboard (ForgeCI, payments-api). The 'Deploy to staging' stage uses a present role="status" cell; on Run deploy a spinner is injected with alt="spinner.gif" (busy) then swapped for a green check with alt="check_24.png" (done). The live region announces the asset filenames instead of the build state.

ruleName: Tallgrass State University LMS course-materials page with a standard APG tablist (Overview / Syllabus & policies / Readings). Selecting a tab hides one role=tabpanel and shows another — new content appears — with deliberately no role=status/aria-live. The content change is exposing/hiding content by interacting with a UI component, governed by 4.1.2, and is excepted from 4.1.3.

Cedar Mesa Pharmacy controlled-substance refill form. Submit fails the early-refill rule and the page (1) opens a role=alertdialog (aria-modal=true) and moves focus into it — a change of context that already announces the error — AND (2) also copies the same error text into a persistent role=alert aria-live=assertive banner outside the dialog. The screen-reader user hears the failure twice. Over-announcement / chattiness failure direction.

Riverside Folk Festival post-event satisfaction survey. Selecting a LOW overall rating ('Poor'/'Very poor') appends conditional follow-up questions (a select + free-text box) without taking focus and with no role=status/aria-live. The appended questions are new form fields, not a status message (they convey no success/waiting/progress/error), so the SC does not apply.

Spanish-language banking two-step verification screen (Banco Aurora, <html lang="es">). After the 6-digit code is submitted, success is shown solely by a green-check <svg role="img" aria-label="check"> injected into a present aria-live="assertive" region — a non-empty name that names the symbol's shape (and is untranslated English) rather than the verification status.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The OTP result container is a pre-existing aria-live='assertive' region that is correctly structured to announce status messages to assistive technology without requiring focus.

ruleName: Olive & Thyme restaurant reservation form. On submit the booking is confirmed without a reload and without moving focus (focus stays on the now-hidden Reserve button). Two things appear: (A) a success line 'Your table is booked…' which IS a status message, and (B) a reservation-details <dl> card (date/time/party/table) which is just booking data, like a results list, and is NOT a status. Neither is in a live region; the silent success line is the failure, the silent details card is fine. False-negative direction distinguished from a non-status list.

Aperture Robotics careers page with a faceted job filter (Department, Location). Filtering runs client-side with no reload and without moving focus. A summary line updates to 'Showing N of 3 open roles.' or 'No roles match your filters.' rendered as a plain
